## M6 — Invariants

Asserted at the end of every fast tick (M4.G.2). A violation **MUST** raise, not warn.

| ID | Invariant | Explainer |
|---|---|---|
| **M6.I.1** | The family undifferentiation budget has exactly **three** sinks and is conserved across them, **reduced only by a completed differentiating exchange** (`M5.D.7`, `M11.C.29`), which is a logged sink | §7 I1 |
| **M6.I.2** | Emotional distance runs **outside** the budget as an always-on baseline; it **MUST NOT** be a fourth sink | §7 I2 |
| **M6.I.3** | `life_energy` is zero-sum per person between relationship-seeking and goal-directed activity | §7 I3 |
| **M6.I.4** | Dyadic exchange conserves **pseudo-self** — defined in 1979 Tape 2 as what is *negotiable*: basic self is what a person believes in and stands by, the position they keep **whatever the pressure**; pseudo-self is belief taken on through schooling, reading and the like, and pressure from others can change it, where it cannot change basic self (`_LECTURES_1979.md` §A5). The negotiability test is the exemption test: one spouse's functional gain equals the other's loss. Borrowed pseudo-self settles back when the exchange stops — on a tie the pair has exchanged on (its functioning balance is not zero), whose over-functioning member carries borrowed pseudo-self and the other lent, and between whom no `OVERFUNCTION` or `UNDERFUNCTION` was sent for `exchange_window` weeks (8, `[I]`), `pseudo_self_relaxation_rate` (0.05, `[I]`) of the smaller of the two moves back from the one who borrowed to the one who lent, with the same of `functional_level`; total pseudo-self is conserved. It is `M1.A.5c`'s "a borrowed rise does not survive withdrawal of the source", and what `M11.C.24` reads. A living person's balance on a tie to the dead settles back as `M6.3e` states, by the same conserved transfer against the dead person's ledger. What an over-functioner takes in one exchange **MUST** be scaled by their own room above the stress floor, `s = clip((f − m) / (b − m), 0, 1)` with the floor `m = max(0, b − stress_floor_below_basic)` (`f` their functional level, `b` their basic level), clamped at 0 as the giver's floor and stress's are: full at or above basic, a third at 10 below for a basic level of 15 or more, none at the floor. It is the mirror of the giver's floor (revision 19), made gradual, and adds no constant. It reads capacity, not the cause of the fall, so a collapse written to the stress ledger reaches the exchange (`M11.C.21`) | §7 I4 |
| **M6.I.4a** | *Lent functioning returns with lost capacity.* Once a week, just before `M6.I.4`'s settling back (update-order step 9), each living person holding borrowed (positive) pseudo-self whose capacity fell over the week by any cause other than `M6.I.4`'s own transfers — a collapse on the stress ledger, a symptom, `M1.A.5f`, `floor_held` shed — **MUST** return to the people who lent it the share of their borrowed pseudo-self equal to the share of capacity lost, `(s_before − s_after) ÷ s_before`, with the same of `functional_level`. `s` is `M6.I.4`'s room above the stress floor, `s = clip((f − m) ÷ (b − m), 0, 1)` with `m = max(0, b − stress_floor_below_basic)` (1 when `b = m` and `f ≥ m`, else 0), read at the week's start (`s_before`) and at this step (`s_after`), with what `M6.I.4`'s transfers moved that week left out of `f`; a person with `s_before` = 0 returns nothing, and so does a fall that stays at or above basic level, where `s` is 1, and a fall in `f` no larger than `invariant_tolerance`, which is the rounding of adding and removing the week's transfers. `pseudo_self` does not record lenders, so it returns to the partners on ties whose functioning balance names this person the over-functioner and who hold lent (negative) pseudo-self, in proportion to what each holds lent, none given back more than they lent nor taken above 100, and the taker not taken below 0; what a cap stops stays with the taker. A dead lender's share is returned against their ledger, as `M6.3e` settles a balance with the dead. Total pseudo-self is conserved. It is the mirror of `M6.I.4`'s capacity scaling of what an over-functioner takes (the owner's form for `M11.C.21`, 2026-10-16), applied to what they hold. It reads capacity, not the cause, and names no projection or child; whether a projection target rises past the arm without collapse (`M11.C.21`) is read, not set. Grade `[I]`, the owner's decision D19 (2026-10-24); no new constant. → `M6.I.4`, `M6.3e`, `M1.A.5c`, `M11.C.21` | §7 I4 |

| **M6.I.6** | Bound anxiety is conserved across transfer events: every change to an anxiety stock is logged against a source, a sink or a transfer named in `M6.4`, and every transfer balances to `M6.1`'s tolerance. Blocking one channel raises flow on the rest. | §7 I6 |
| **M6.I.7** | There is no exit from the field; `CUTOFF`, `DISTANCE` and silence are moves *inside* the system | §7 I7 |
| **M6.I.8** | The standing load runs before delivery, every tick, on every tie | §7.2 — *this spec elevates it to an invariant; the explainer describes it as a mechanism* |

**M6.1** M6.I.1 conservation **MUST** be asserted to a stated tolerance, declared in config, and the tolerance **MUST** be `[I]`.

**M6.2** M6.I.6 **MUST** be assertable across a removal event specifically (M11.C.11).

**M6.4** — *the stock-and-flow table `M6.I.6` asserts.* Every anxiety stock, its sources and sinks, and the transfers that **MUST** balance. A change to a stock by anything not in this table **MUST** raise. `test_m6i6_transfers_balance_every_tick` asserts the transfer column each tick; `test_m64_every_stock_change_is_logged_by_name` asserts that every source and sink is logged by name.

| Stock | Sources (create) | Sinks (remove) | Transfers (balance) |
|---|---|---|---|

The budget and anxiety are separate stocks; the transfers above are the only stated relation between them. If a later revision takes up `M1.D.1`'s sinks, this table changes with it.

**M6.3** — *disposition at death.* `M6` **MUST** name the mechanism that removes a Person at death, and **MUST** state where that Person's acute and chronic anxiety, bond energy on each tie, functioning-balance debts, `investment`, triangle positions and share of the undifferentiation budget go, so that `M6.I.6` and `M6.I.7` remain assertable across a death. If births occur within the horizon, the creating mechanism and the initial state it assigns **MUST** be named likewise, and `M1.A.20`'s identifier rule applies. **The disposition itself is an owner decision**; the owner decided it on 2026-10-13, and revision 28 states it below. The owner's guidance of 2026-09-22, not yet a requirement: relationship energy behaves like chemical bond energy and does not disappear when a person dies — which agrees with `M1.B.4` (bond energy decays at or near zero) and `M6.I.7` (no exit from the field). `M11.C.37` is the test. → `model_explainer.md` §18 · C15

The owner (2026-10-13): "Every family member has some 'tie' with anxiety bound up to the dead person. The dead person has some level of chronic anxiety. Like chemical bond energy — it gets redistributed. A death is a stressor on individuals as well … If that person was an income source that source is now gone and that's a stressor … everyone's stress going up 'stresses' the system reciprocally. [Grief] dissipate[s] over 1–3 years. Finances have to get resolved somehow." And on finances: "family members have to find a job. They have to figure it out for themselves. Trying equals finding, but at 20% less income." `M6.3a`–`M6.3i` are the disposition, applied in this order in the week of the death. The forms are Claude's reading.

**M6.3a** — *the mechanism.* A death is an exogenous event drawn by `M7.C.1j`. The dead person **MUST** stop selecting, perceiving and appraising, and their ties **MUST** stay in the state, non-interactive (`M6.I.7`). Bond energy on a tie to the dead **MUST** stay where it is (`M1.B.4`): what the owner's "redistributed" moves is anxiety (`M6.3b`).

**M6.3b** — *the dead person's anxiety goes to the living, in proportion to the ties.* The dead person's whole `acute_anxiety` stock, whose floor is their chronic anxiety, **MUST** be split among the living family members on ties to them (`role = MEMBER`; an external agent takes no share), in proportion to each tie's bond energy, and added to their acute anxiety. It is a transfer in `M6.4`. (`death_transfer_share` is 1. No criterion overrides it: `M11.C.15` keeps the transfer; only `M11.C.37`'s mutation sets it lower.) If no living family member holds a tie to the dead, the stock **MUST** be split equally among the living members of the dead person's household, and failing those, among all living family members. Grief (`M6.3g`) likewise reaches family members only.

**M6.3c** — *what the dead person's ties and triangles held.* Tie-bound anxiety (`M1.D.2a`) on a tie to the dead **MUST** go to the tie's living member. A triangle with the dead as a member **MUST** discharge its bound anxiety equally to its living members and dissolve. The dead person's `symptom_bound` (`M7.D.2a`) **MUST** go back to the partners, as when a symptom ends. An external agent who is a symptom partner or a triangle member receives its share under this clause; only `M6.3b`'s share of the dead person's own acute anxiety excludes them (the owner, 2026-10-14: "okay").

**M6.3d** — *investment.* Each living person's `investment` in the tie to the dead **MUST** be redistributed over their other interactive ties, in proportion to what each already holds: `M7.C.1a`'s conserved budget, run in reverse.

**M6.3e** — *functioning balances.* On a tie to the dead, the living person's borrowed or lent pseudo-self **MUST** settle back toward zero at revision 27's rate (`M6.I.4`). It is the same conserved transfer, against the dead person's ledger, which no longer acts or is read, so total pseudo-self stays conserved. An overfunctioner whose underfunctioning partner dies loses the borrowed self (`M11.C.15`); an underfunctioner whose overfunctioning partner dies recovers what was lent (`kerr_book/ks22.md` · KS22.8, the projection target improving after both parents died).

**M6.3f** — *the family's budget.* A sink allocation that named the dead (spouse dysfunction carried by them, child projection onto them) **MUST** return to its family as on `binder_unavailable` (`M1.F.9`). When both spouses of a family are dead, the family **MUST** stop taking allocations; its budget is kept and logged, not moved. The allocation is per sink, not per child, so a dead child returns the family's whole child-projection allocation; and acts with someone since dead no longer draw the budget.

**M6.3g** — *grief.* Each living family member on an interactive tie to the dead (an inactive holder is not one) **MUST** receive a lasting stressor (`M1.F.6`) sized by `M1.F.6a` — `GRIEF` at 100 LCU for a spouse (a marital tie to the dead) and 63 for any other family member, at reach `bond_energy ÷ 100`, times `grief_weight` (1.0, `[I]`) — delivered over its weeks, lasting `52 + 104 × bond_energy ÷ 100` weeks: one year on the weakest tie and three on the strongest (the owner's "1–3 years").

**M6.3h** — *lost income.* If the dead person was an earner (`Person.earner`, declared in the family config and set by `FIND_WORK`, `M7.C.1k`), each living member of their household **MUST** receive a lasting stressor of intensity `income_loss_intensity` (15, `[I]`) with no end. When a member of the household takes `FIND_WORK` (`M7.C.1k`), the stressor **MUST** fall to 20% of its intensity and stay (the owner: "at 20% less income"), and the actor **MUST** become an earner and not financially dependent (`M1.A.15`, `M7.A.1a`). No rule restores the income. *This amends `M1.F.6` for this one stressor:* its first part ends with an act, not a declared duration, and the remaining 20% has no end, because the owner states that the lower income lasts.

**M6.3i** — *the rest is not a rule.* "Everyone's stress going up stresses the system reciprocally" **MUST NOT** be written as a rule: the raised anxiety reaches the others through the ties (`M4.A`, `M4.C`) as any other does.

**What `M11.C.37` checks.** The family's total anxiety is conserved across `M6.3b` and `M6.3c`. Grief and lost income are sources logged after the disposition and are outside that check.
